Olga (Contractor - Remote): hey team, thinking about moving my base from Ukraine to Tallinn in July. i'm an external contractor now. want to know: can i keep contractor status while on e-residency, will the monthly contractor allowance continue, and does having an e-resident contractor create an Estonian tax/VAT/employer exposure for Redwood?
Sam (People Ops): short answer: e-residency != automatic employment. but local rules vary. main q: will you remain contractor with your client agreements or switch to FT?
Olga (Contractor - Remote): plan is to stay contractor and invoice Redwood from an Estonian company i'm setting up using e-residency. already started the company registration.
Ivo (Payroll EMEA): operational note: if you invoice from an Estonian corporate entity, Redwood treats you as a vendor, not payroll. contractor allowance historically paid to ICs can continue as part of invoices, but we'll need valid invoices and VAT treatment.
Tax EMEA: flags: if Redwood has an Estonian-registered supplier (your company) and you provide services from Estonia, VAT reverse-charge rules may apply depending on VAT registration. also, having an individual working physically in Estonia might create a permanent establishment only if there are contract-signing or sustained client-facing activities. single contractor usually doesn't change corporate tax status, but we need to confirm substance.
Legal EMEA: please be careful: local labor authorities sometimes reclassify long-term contractor relationships as employment if work resembles employee duties. keep contracts clear and avoid employee-like controls (set hours, reporting lines). we'll review your new contractor agreement draft.
Olga (Contractor - Remote): ok. about the contractor allowance ($250/mo): can I keep receiving it? I currently get it as a separate invoice line.
Sam (People Ops): yes invoices can include the allowance. just ensure invoice line items match services and costs. if your Estonian company is VAT-registered, add VAT per Estonian rules; Redwood will handle reverse-charge where applicable.
Olga (Contractor - Remote): will Redwood need to register for Estonian VAT or payroll because of me?
Tax EMEA: unlikely just for one vendor, but if Redwood starts having a fixed place of business or hires employees in EE, that triggers registration. invoicing from your Estonian company normally doesn't force Redwood registration, but we will do a quick nexus check once your company is active.
Ivo (Payroll EMEA): practical: if you later convert to employee, payroll onboarding would require employer setup in EE. for now we process as vendor. please send company reg docs and VAT number when ready.
Olga (Contractor - Remote): got it. any data/security requirements for working from Estonia?
Legal EMEA: same company policies apply (IP assignment, NDA, data handling). e-residency doesn't change security rules. keep device encryption and sign the contractor addendum we shared.
Olga (Contractor - Remote): i'll share company reg and VAT once done. do i need to change my contractor country in the vendor portal?
Sam (People Ops): yes, update vendor profile to Estonia and attach W-8/other tax docs as applicable. Folks in vendor ops will confirm withholding needs.
PeopleOpsBot: "Case #R-6244 created and assigned to Sam. Reminder: vendor onboarding checklist posted in the case"
Tax EMEA: final note: we recommend a short call with our external tax advisor to confirm VAT reverse-charge mechanics and confirm there's no payroll/employer trigger. i'll schedule if you want.
Olga (Contractor - Remote): please do, that would help. thanks everyone :slightly_smiling_face:
